name: Aviation Maintenance Technology
description: Aviation maintenance programmes prepare people to inspect, repair and sign off aircraft — airframes, engines, hydraulics, electrical and the inspections that keep an aircraft legal to fly. ⚠ Unlike every other trade programme on this site, the curriculum is set by the FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION rather than by Florida.
degreesNote: The destination is the FAA mechanic certificate with Airframe and Powerplant ratings — the “A&P” — and a programme exists to get you there. ⚠⚠ The school itself must be certificated by the FAA under 14 CFR Part 147; graduating from one is what lets you sit the tests without the alternative route of 18 months of documented experience for a single rating, or 30 months for both. ⚠ Florida institutions deliver it two ways: as clock-hour career certificates (general, airframe and powerplant blocks of 450–480 hours each) and, at a few colleges, as college-credit courses inside an associate degree. Both lead to the same federal certificate; the difference is the transcript and what else it counts toward.

cips.note: Airframe mechanics and aircraft maintenance technology — 13 Florida public institutions, 297 credentials in 2023.
Aircraft powerplant technology — 11 institutions, 178 credentials. ⚠ Filed separately from airframe because the FAA rates them separately, and a student can hold one without the other.

related.note: ⚠ The comparison worth making before you choose: both are diagnostic mechanical trades taught at the same technical colleges, but aviation is federally certificated, pays roughly half again as much at the median, and is far more tied to documentation.
Where an A&P goes next without leaving aviation: avionics, non-destructive testing and aviation maintenance management all sit in the engineering-technology series.
